## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Suhanujātaka* (Ja 158) is a narrative belonging to the Pali Jātaka collection [SuttaCentral]. In the edition of the commentary by V. Fausböll, it is situated as the eighth story of its vagga, opening with the canonical verse beginning *Na-y-idam visamasīlena* [Fausböll 1879]. 

The framing narrative (*paccuppannavatthu*) is set at Jetavana, where the Buddha delivers the teaching concerning two hot-tempered, violent monks (*dve caṇḍabhikkhū*) [SuttaCentral; Fausböll 1879]. In the tale of the past (*atītavatthu*), horse dealers troubled by a vicious royal horse named Mahāsoṇa consult the Bodhisatta, who serves as a wise minister (*paṇḍitāmacco*) to the king [Fausböll 1879]. The Bodhisatta instructs them to bring another notoriously fierce horse named Suhanu from their home city to confront it [Fausböll 1879]. In the concluding identification (*samodhāna*), the Buddha reveals that the two unruly horses were the two hot-tempered monks, the king was Ānanda, and the wise minister was the Bodhisatta himself [Fausböll 1879].

SuttaCentral lists four translations of the text in four modern languages [SuttaCentral]. Neither curated parallels nor automated cross-language matches (with score ≥ 10) or internal Pali text reuse are recorded for this jātaka by SuttaCentral or DharmaNexus [SuttaCentral; DharmaNexus].
